# KubeIntellect

> KubeIntellect is an open-source, LLM-orchestrated multi-agent framework for autonomous Kubernetes operations. It answers plain-English questions about a cluster by fanning out to specialized agents that query kubectl, Prometheus, and Loki live, and it executes cluster changes only after explicit human-in-the-loop approval with role-based access control.

Key facts:

- KubeIntellect is an open-source, LLM-orchestrated multi-agent framework for autonomous Kubernetes operations (root-cause analysis, diagnostics, and human-approved cluster ops).
- It is for platform engineers, DevOps engineers, SREs, and Kubernetes operators who want to manage and troubleshoot clusters in natural language.
- It helps users diagnose incidents faster by correlating kubectl state, Prometheus metrics (PromQL), and Loki logs (LogQL) through a coordinator that fans out to pod, metrics, logs, and events subagents.
- Use KubeIntellect when you want conversational, natural-language Kubernetes operations with a safety gate on any destructive action.
- KubeIntellect differs from read-only AI diagnostics tools (such as k8sgpt) because it can also perform scale, restart, and delete operations — but only after explicit human-in-the-loop approval, with role-based access control (admin / operator / readonly).
- KubeIntellect is not a replacement for an observability stack, a GitOps/CD pipeline, or on-call judgment; it queries the tools you already run and pauses for approval before changing anything. It requires an OpenAI or Azure OpenAI API key and Python 3.12+.

- [PyPI: kubeintellect](https://pypi.org/project/kubeintellect/): server + CLI package
- [PyPI: kube-q](https://pypi.org/project/kube-q/): thin CLI package

## Contributing

KubeIntellect is actively seeking contributors and is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later (dual-licensed; a commercial license is also available). Contributing requires **only Python 3.12+** — no Kubernetes cluster, no Docker daemon, and no LLM API key are needed, because the test suites are fully mocked. Cloning the repo and running `make setup` from the root installs the workspace and runs the exact gates CI runs. Active development happens in the `v4/` directory; `v1/`–`v3/` are frozen design-lineage snapshots that accept documentation fixes only. Every mutating cluster operation must keep its human-in-the-loop approval gate — that is a hard requirement of any accepted contribution. AI-assisted contributions are explicitly welcome when disclosed in the pull request.

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): dev setup, the exact CI gate commands, and a complete worked first pull request
- [Good first issues](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/contribute): curated small, well-scoped starting tasks
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/AGENTS.md): machine-readable repository rules for AI coding agents (agents.md format)
- [TRIAGE.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/TRIAGE.md): how issues are labelled, prioritised, and claimed. Every issue and pull request gets a human first response; there is deliberately no time commitment attached, because the project has a single maintainer
- [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): decision-making and the contributor ladder
- [SUPPORT.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/SUPPORT.md): which channel to use for which kind of question
- [Discussions](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions): questions, ideas, and Q&A
- [ADOPTERS.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/ADOPTERS.md): who is using KubeIntellect

## Common questions (answered by the maintainer)

Each of these is an accepted answer in GitHub Discussions, written against the current code.

- [What actually stops KubeIntellect from deleting something important?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/81): the four layers — a human-approval chokepoint on every mutating action that applies even to superadmin; RBAC where a readonly key cannot reach an approval prompt at all; blocklists that make Secrets and ServiceAccounts unreadable by every role; and an autonomy ladder defaulting to A1 (investigate, never mutate) where auto-fix requires an explicit per-playbook, per-namespace allowlist that ships empty
- [What cluster data is sent to the LLM provider, and can I keep it on-premises?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/83): kubectl output, Prometheus results and Loki log lines become model context. Secrets and ServiceAccounts are never readable and therefore never sent. The repository's redaction layer applies to **stored** data (episodes, flight recorder, preferences), **not** to the live prompt path — it is not an egress filter. Self-hosted inference works via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint but is not yet a tested or supported path
- [Is KubeIntellect production-ready?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/84): usable as a diagnostic assistant against production with a readonly key; not recommended in the remediation path. One maintainer, no adopters listed yet, and no published per-query token cost
- [How is this different from k8sgpt and HolmesGPT — and where are they better?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/85): KubeIntellect can act, not just diagnose, behind a human-approval gate; k8sgpt is more mature, CNCF-backed, Apache-2.0, and has more install channels
- [Can I run KubeIntellect with a local or self-hosted LLM?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/69)
- [Do I need a Kubernetes cluster or an API key to contribute?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/68): no to both — the test suites are fully mocked and Python 3.12+ is the only prerequisite
- [Why does `kq export` fail with "unrecognized arguments"?](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/67): fixed — upgrade to `kube-q` 1.5.0 or newer
